title: Introduce lightweight presubmit sieve and dependency-entropy sweeper
author: Priya Kapoor
description:
Problem: Our presubmit lanes are heavy and frequently run a large surface of lint/test jobs even for trivial doc or single-file typos. Separately, dependency churn has been causing transient CI failures and noisy alerts. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: (1) a lightweight presubmit 'sieve' that quickly classifies changes into light/medium/heavy lanes so small changes get fast feedback, and (2) a dependency-entropy sweeper tool that scans PRs for noisy transitive dep changes and suggests minimal lockfile edits.

What this PR does (summary): compresses fast-feedback checks into a new fastpath workflow; adds a small Go-based dep-sweeper binary invoked as an optional presubmit step; wires a conditional lint-router that dispatches to the appropriate job profile; updates docs and CI templates; provides a migration guide for teams that want to opt into strict dep-sweeper gating.

Why now: reducing developer wait time by 40-60% on trivial PRs was flagged as a top pain point (ENG-2120). Simultaneously, spike analysis showed ~12% of flaky CI failures originate from lockfile churn across package managers. The sweeper helps reduce noise and surfaces minimal actionable changes.

Checklist:
- [x] Add presubmit-sieve workflow and fastpath job definitions
- [x] Implement dep-sweeper (Go) and integrate in CI as opt-in check
- [x] Add documentation and migration notes (docs/ci/presubmit.md)
- [x] Add unit tests for dep-sweeper and integration smoke test for conditional routing
- [x] Run dogfood on two internal repos for one week

Migration notes: The new sieve is opt-in by default for all repos; repo owners can flip the presubmit profile via .github/presubmit-profile.yaml. The dep-sweeper emits a JSON summary but does not block merges until enabled by repository policy. To enable strict gating, add label ci/strict-deps to your repo config.

Rollback plan: Remove workflow or set sieve to 'always-heavy' in repo config. Dep-sweeper is non-blocking until enabled, so rollback is low risk.

review_comments: Evan Miller (reviewer): Can we keep the fastpath job resource footprint intentionally tiny? Suggest limiting matrix/containers to 1 to avoid scheduling delay.
Priya Kapoor (author): Good call — reduced fastpath to a single lightweight container and added a comment in presubmit-sieve.yaml explaining the rationale.
Sofia Ramirez (reviewer): The dep-sweeper output looks useful, but can we avoid JSON noise in logs? Consider writing summary to artifacts instead of stdout.
Priya Kapoor (author): Updated sweeper to write condensed summary to /tmp/dep-sweeper-summary.json and uploaded as a CI artifact; kept full verbose dump behind --debug flag.
Liam Chen (reviewer): Please add a short integration smoke test that exercises a benign lockfile change to ensure the sweeper doesn't crash on unexpected formats.
Priya Kapoor (author): Added tests/integration/presubmit-sieve/smoke.sh and CI step that runs it on a small fixture.
release_notes: Adds an opt-in presubmit 'sieve' workflow for fast-feedback on small changes and a non-blocking dependency-entropy sweeper that surfaces minimal lockfile edits. Docs and example configs included.
testing_summary: Dogfooded on internal/service-a and internal/sdk-python for 7 days. Fastpath reduced median presubmit runtime from ~8m to ~2.5m for trivial PRs. Dep-sweeper flagged 18 noisy lockfile edits; teams adopted suggestions in 12 cases, reducing CI flakes in those repos.
notes_for_ops: When enabling strict dep gating, ensure org-level artifact retention allows the dep-sweeper summary to be retained for 7 days. Monitor presubmit-sieve fastpath runner utilization for first 2 weeks.
impact_estimate: Medium - improves developer productivity and reduces CI noise; introduces a small Go binary (no runtime infra change).
